standard.title: Interpret Information and Data
standard.description: interpret information and data to identify economic and business issues, trends and economic cause-and-effect relationships
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can evaluate information and data to identify and describe patterns and trends, and infer relationships (AC9HS6S03). The Year 7 demand adds specific economic frames — identifying issues, identifying multi-variable trends using interactive digital tools, and reasoning about cause-and-effect relationships in economic contexts.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students interpret information and data to identify economic and business issues, trends and economic cause-and-effect relationships.

nodes.label: Identifying economic issues from information
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can interpret information to identify an economic or business issue, making an inference beyond what is directly stated.
nodes.minimum_width: Interpret one piece of economic information and identify the issue it points to; explain the inference made.
nodes.typical_width: Interpret information from a range of sources to identify economic and business issues; make inferences beyond the data — for example, inferring the effect of growth in online shopping on the number of customers entering physical stores.
wider: Interpret multiple pieces of information about the same economic issue from sources with different perspectives (e.g. business data vs consumer survey) and explain how each reveals a different aspect of the issue
Identify an economic issue affecting a First Nations community by interpreting community economic data or a published community report
Examine a news article or data release and identify two distinct economic issues it raises — practising the separation of connected issues
nodes.hinge_reason: Students who can only describe what data shows — without inferring the issue behind it — will not be able to engage with trend identification or cause-and-effect reasoning in subsequent nodes. Interpretation that stops at 'what happened' cannot advance to 'what issue does this reveal or what caused it.'

response_modes.reason: Students need an explicit inference scaffold: 'The data shows X. This suggests Y is happening. The economic issue this points to is Z.' Practise the move from data observation to issue identification before asking students to do it independently.

success_criteria: Identifies an economic or business issue from provided information
Explains the inference made — what in the information pointed to the issue

nodes.label: Identifying trends using multi-variable data
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can interpret multi-variable data using interactive digital tools to identify trends and answer specific questions about economic change over time.
nodes.minimum_width: Use a provided digital tool to identify one trend in a two-variable economic dataset; describe the trend in economic terms.
nodes.typical_width: Interpret multi-variable data using interactive digital tools — identifying trends, answering directed questions such as 'For a 10-year period, how has the number of people in casual work changed?'; explain what the trend reveals about the economic context.
wider: Compare trends across two different time periods or demographic groups in the same dataset — identifying whether a trend is consistent or variable
Select an appropriate digital tool to investigate a self-directed trend question about a contemporary economic issue, justifying the tool and dataset choice
Interpret employment trend data disaggregated by gender or regional area and identify what this reveals about differential economic participation

response_modes.reason: Students need experience with multiple dataset types and digital tools before they can apply trend identification independently. Build fluency through a sequence of increasingly complex datasets — starting with simple two-variable line graphs, progressing to multi-variable interactive displays.

success_criteria: Identifies and describes a trend in a multi-variable dataset using a digital tool
Answers a directed question about the trend using evidence from the data

nodes.label: Cause-and-effect relationships
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can interpret visual displays of multi-variable data to identify a cause-and-effect relationship within an economic issue, such as the relationship between income and saving or spending behaviour.
nodes.minimum_width: Identify one cause-and-effect relationship in a visual display of economic data; explain which variable is the cause and which is the effect.
nodes.typical_width: Interpret visual displays of multi-variable data to identify cause-and-effect relationships — for example, the relationship between income and levels of saving and spending; explain the direction and nature of the relationship using evidence from the data; distinguish correlation from causation.
wider: Analyse a case where an apparent economic cause-and-effect relationship is complicated by a third variable — practising the distinction between correlation and causation
Investigate a cause-and-effect relationship in the context of a First Nations community economic issue — for example, how access to financial services affects saving behaviour in remote communities
Compare cause-and-effect relationships in consumer behaviour data across different demographic groups, identifying what additional variables might explain differences

response_modes.reason: Cause-and-effect reasoning in economics requires students to hold the relationship structure in mind: 'X changes, which causes Y to change, because...' The 'because' is the economic reasoning. Students need scaffolded practice constructing the full chain, not just labelling the correlation.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Economic cause-and-effect relationships vary meaningfully across contexts — income and spending, employment type and financial security, access to services and economic outcomes. Broader context exposure builds transferable causal reasoning rather than surface-level data description.
success_criteria: Identifies a cause-and-effect relationship in a visual data display
Explains the direction of the relationship using evidence from the data
Uses economic terms (trend, cause, effect, relationship, variable) accurately
